title: 3DGraphX: Explaining 3D Molecular Graph Models via Incorporating Chemical Priors

problem.claim: The work addresses explanation of 3D graph neural networks in molecular learning.

gap.claim: Existing 2D GNN explanation methods do not address the formidable challenges of explaining 3D graphs and their molecular geometries.

contributions.claim: 3DGraphX is a paradigm for explaining 3D molecular graph models by focusing on chemically meaningful 3D motifs.
The method provides instance-level explanations through mask pooling and mask unpooling components that discover important motifs for each 3D molecule.
The method provides geometry-level explanations using local spherical coordinate systems to investigate relative motif positions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe 3DGraphX and its methods and components as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that fixing generated 3D motifs in the explanation model produces more accurate and chemically plausible explanations efficiently.
Experimental results reportedly show that 3DGraphX significantly outperforms baselines for instance-level explanation across various explanation budgets.
Additional experiments reportedly show that 3DGraphX reveals important geometries used by 3D GNNs for accurate molecular learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper targets explanation of 3D GNNs for molecular learning.
The authors identify challenges in explaining 3D molecular graphs and distinguish the setting from existing 2D explanation methods.
3DGraphX uses fixed 3D motifs and has separate instance-level and geometry-level explanation branches.
Mask pooling and unpooling discover important motifs, while local spherical coordinates describe relative motif positions.
The authors report improved instance-level explanation against baselines and discovery of important geometries for molecular learning.

source_observation.claim: The method fixes chemically meaningful 3D motifs before producing explanations.

interpretation.claim: Constraining explanations with domain-relevant structures may improve plausibility and efficiency.

application.claim: For structured scientific data, explanation systems could incorporate stable domain motifs or units as explanation primitives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether fixed motifs are suitable when the relevant structures are unknown or highly variable.

source_observation.claim: 3DGraphX separates instance-level motif discovery from geometry-level analysis.

interpretation.claim: Different explanation targets may require distinct mechanisms rather than one unified attribution representation.

application.claim: Explanation designs can separate identification of important components from analysis of their spatial or relational arrangement.

exception.claim: The abstract does not show whether the two explanation levels are jointly optimized or how their outputs should be reconciled.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baseline identities, evaluation metrics, or quantitative performance values.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for motif generation, mask pooling, mask unpooling, or geometry analysis.
The abstract does not establish the scope of molecular tasks or the limits of the reported findings.
